decision: Test kernels are booted from their EFI image (vmlinuz.efi), and the conveyor refuses anything else.
why: A gzip kernel was chosen by the bootloader, counted down, and could not start - silently, before any log.
rejected: Sort keys, a stored default entry, a second boot partition - each checked and ruled out.

decision: The audio pin driver's function slots for the SoundWire pins follow the phone's own Android kernel (gpio19 swr_tx_data in slot 3, gpio23 swr_rx_data in slot 2).
why: A bus clash on the TX bus came right before the codec's timeout; the driver's table disagreed with the vendor's pin description on exactly these pins; corrected, the codec came up on the first boot.
rejected: Treating the clocks switching off as the cause; changing the macros' autosuspend.

decision: Boots that come up without the sound card are measured over a run of reboots before anything is changed.
why: It happened once in several boots; the audio processor's service channel never appeared. A guess at a cause would be untestable without a rate.
rejected: Unmasking the helper service masked for the suspend crash, on a hunch.

decision: With the SIM in, the modem is examined read-only first; switching the radio on is the only change made, and nothing that calls, messages or uses data happens without the author's word.
why: A SIM card costs money and reaches people; the phone's state stays known.
rejected: Trying a call or a data connection straight away.

decision: The capture failure is not chased in runtime power management.
why: With the bus controllers, macros, codec and SoundWire devices all forced awake, the read failure came at the same moment, the same way.
rejected: Changing the macros' autosuspend or the controller's clock-stop handling.

decision: The right channel is the bottom speaker.
why: With the microphone at the bottom speaker the right channel read 7 dB louder (-20.4 against -27.6 dBFS; room -85.7).
rejected: An earlier 2 dB lean, taken while the microphone was not yet placed.

decision: Where the community's report and our measurement disagree, both are shown side by side; where we know nothing, the report is shown outlined, dated, as reported.
why: A disagreement is the most telling part of the comparison - the sensors one may be of our own making.
rejected: Hiding a report behind our measurement; filling unknowns as if measured.

decision: Telephony is checked in three modes: automatic now (registration; a small download over mobile data), half-manual (the phone calls the author's other phone, the author confirms through the inbox), and fully automatic later (a two-phone stand, or a number that answers with a tone). The number to call lives in a private file on the lab machine, never in a repository.
why: The author allowed data and calls to his other phone, and asked that the checks become part of the test suite so a stand can run them unattended.
rejected: Calls by hand without a check; keeping the number in the device manifest.
